name: validate-email
summary: Validate whether a string is a syntactically well-formed email address.
description: Checks structural validity of an email address (local-part@domain shape, character classes, length, dot placement) against a simplified, deterministic ruleset -- not full RFC 5321/5322 grammar and not a deliverability check. Does not perform DNS/MX lookups, does not verify the mailbox exists, and does not attempt SMTP verification, since none of those are possible from inside the capability sandbox (no network access) and would be non-deterministic even if they were. Whitespace is not trimmed by this capability -- callers must trim input themselves; a leading/trailing space is treated as an invalid character and reported as such. Plus-addressing (`user+tag@domain`) is treated as valid by default per the `allow_plus_addressing` input field.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the email field, possibly empty.

postconditions.description: Returns valid: true only if the string matches the documented simplified email-shape ruleset; otherwise valid: false with a non-null reason explaining which rule failed.
Never performs DNS/MX/SMTP verification -- valid: true means structurally well-formed, not that the mailbox exists or accepts mail.

side_effects.description: Produces one validation result derived from the provided email string; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.
